_comment: Where the game's real internal item names are read from, before we have the
game files.
WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Hard rule 3 of this project is that the
internal snake_case name is the key, always — numeric ids change between
patches. Until now every item id was `toSnakeId(displayName)`, a provisional
guess, and every guess that differs from the real name is an error that is
invisible today and expensive later: user progress in IndexedDB is keyed by
these ids, so a rename after release orphans somebody's museum tracker.
THE SOURCE. AnnaNomoly's DigUpAnything mod ships a table of 1,906 rows —
numeric id, internal name, displayed name — read out of the game at v0.15.0.
It is a factual identifier mapping, not prose, and it is used here to derive
our own alias table rather than being copied wholesale. Attribution is in
docs/DATA-POLICY.md.
https://github.com/AnnaNomoly/legacy-fields-of-mistria-mods
WHY THE MATCH IS ON DISPLAY NAME. It is the only column the wiki and this
table share. A display name that appears twice is therefore useless for
matching and is dropped rather than resolved arbitrarily — the conflict is
reported instead.
STALE, NOT WRONG. v0.15.0 predates 1.0, so a matched name is recorded as
`confirmed_stale`, never `confirmed`. It is a large improvement on a slug and
still something the game files will settle at G1. Every item that changes id
keeps its old one in `former_ids`, which is what makes that settlement a
migration rather than a data loss.
MARKERS. Rows the mod marks DISABLED, GLITCHED or PLACEHOLDER are content
that does not work in game. They are kept in the source snapshot and excluded
from matching, because adopting the id of a crashing item would be adopting a
name for something the player can never hold.
_marker_comment: Notes-column markers that mean the row is not a usable item.
_missing_comment: The mod writes this where an item has no displayed name at all.
